transcutaneous stimulation of the efferent fibers of the vagus nerve is a safe, effective and feasible treatment option for the treatment of patients with sepsis, and that this treatment option should be further evaluated in a clinical setting.
transcutaneous electrical vagus nerve activation is able to reduce systemic levels of inflammatory cytokines and HMGB1 and to improve survival in septic mice.
vagus nerve stimulation is an effective treatment for the prevention and reversal of endotoxin- and sepsis-induced organ dysfunction, and that this effect is mediated by the release of acetylcholine.
